name: Sigmoid
tagline: Scroll motion without the JavaScript tax: native CSS scroll timelines, spring and S-curve easings as CSS linear(), reduced motion by default. About 3 kB for a reveal.
seoTitle: Sigmoid – scroll-driven animations and spring easing for CSS and React
description:
Most scroll animations still run in JavaScript: a listener measures elements and changes styles on every frame. Browsers can now do this themselves with CSS scroll-driven animations. Sigmoid is a small layer on top of that platform feature. Reveals, parallax and scroll-linked effects run on native view and scroll timelines, and a tiny fallback with the same range maths covers browsers that do not have them yet.

With `sigmoid.css` you do not even need JavaScript: write `data-sigmoid="fade-up"` and the browser animates it. The easing curves are the other half: physically correct springs, the logistic S-curve and Bézier curves that work as JavaScript functions and as CSS `linear()`, also together with Motion, GSAP or Tailwind. When people ask their system for reduced motion, Sigmoid shows the content without moving it.

faq.q: Why not just use Motion or GSAP?
faq.a: Both are excellent and do far more: layout animations, gestures, timelines. If you only need scroll-linked motion and good curves, Sigmoid lets the browser do the work and stays around 3 kB. Its easing curves also work inside Motion and GSAP.

faq.q: How does it compare in size and speed?
faq.a: A reveal is about 3 kB, GSAP with ScrollTrigger about 45 kB and Motion about 23 kB, all minified and gzipped. On a native timeline Sigmoid runs about 1 ms of JavaScript while scrolling. With hundreds of elements animating at once, Chromium's native path costs more main-thread time than GSAP in our headless test, and we say so in the benchmark. The script is in the repository.

Browsers with CSS scroll-driven animations, such as Chrome, Edge and Safari 26. Others, Firefox for now, get the JavaScript fallback with the same result. CI checks both paths in real Chromium, Firefox and WebKit on every change. The docs list the details.

faq.q: Is there a Vue or Svelte package?
faq.a: Yes. @sweberdev/sigmoid-vue has the v-reveal and v-parallax directives and composables, @sweberdev/sigmoid-svelte has the actions use:reveal, use:parallax, use:track and use:story. Install either next to @sweberdev/sigmoid. Astro needs no adapter, the docs have a guide.

faq.q: Does it work with Next.js and Server Components?
faq.a: Yes. The data-sigmoid attributes work in Server Components without client code. The React components are client components that render one element.
Reveals and parallax are skipped and the content is shown. Only the reading progress bar stays, because it moves only when the user scrolls.
